title: Restore missing Beads metadata so embedded Dolt resolves correctly
description:
## Summary
Beads in the Streets repo stopped working because the repo-local .beads metadata files were missing. Without them, bd fell back to the default embedded database name 'beads' instead of the actual embedded database 'streets', which caused status and other commands to fail.

## Symptoms
- bd status failed trying to open .beads\\embeddeddolt\\beads\\.dolt\\repo_state.json
- bd context resolved database 'beads' instead of 'streets'
- The repo should use the uc- issue prefix and embedded Dolt mode

## Acceptance Criteria
- bd context reports backend dolt with dolt_mode embedded
- bd resolves database 'streets'
- Streets issue IDs use the uc- prefix
- The resolution is documented in this bead
notes:
Root cause and resolution will be added after validation.
Validated root cause: .beads/config.yaml and .beads/metadata.json were missing, so bd fell back to the default embedded database name 'beads'. The actual embedded database for this repo is 'streets', and the repo identity also requires the stored project_id b25f25c4-ffe9-4ef0-ba57-98e0e87395e3. Safe repair applied: recreated .beads/config.yaml with issue-prefix 'uc' and the repo sync.remote, recreated .beads/metadata.json with backend=dolt, dolt_mode=embedded, dolt_database=streets, and the matching project_id from the live database. Verification: bd context --json now reports backend=dolt, dolt_mode=embedded, database=streets; bd where resolves to .beads/embeddeddolt; bd list and bd status succeed again. No reinstall, reinit, cleanup, or destructive repair commands were used.
close_reason: Restored missing Beads metadata, reattached the repo to the embedded Dolt database 'streets', confirmed uc- prefix resolution, and verified bd commands work again.

notes:
Decision confirmed: private 'agent-tooling' repo is the canonical home. Rationale: Streets already has three public repos; PT Tracker is on its fourth build after agents repeatedly deferred infrastructure ('you're not big enough for this yet') — resulting in Firebase seams failures, >5k-line static index files, and a JS-to-TS migration. The workspace-sibling suggestion from Claude was wrong here. Co-location assumptions and file: links are fragile exactly when you need them most. A private repo enforces a clean consumption contract (devDependency via registry or git URL), survives solo checkouts, and treats shared tooling as a first-class artifact from the start.

title: Consider blanket --fix flag for preflight auto-resolvable errors
description: Currently preflight has --write for body line wrapping and Biome has its own --write. Consider a single --fix flag on commit:preflight that auto-resolves everything it can: body line wrapping, Biome fixable errors (re-stage), and any other automatically resolvable failures. Agent runs one command and gets the furthest possible toward a clean commit without manual intervention.
notes:
Full design brief for implementer:

WHAT --fix SHOULD DO (in order):
1. Run Biome --write on staged files, restage them (same as commit hook)
2. Wrap body lines at 72 chars using the smart wrapBodyLines (preserves bullet/list indent)
3. Rerun full preflight validation on the resulting state
4. Report a summary of what was auto-applied vs what still needs manual work

WHAT IT SHOULD NOT DO:
- Should not attempt to fix commitlint subject-case violations (rewriting the title is agent intent)
- Should not attempt to fix missing Beads ID (agent must supply this deliberately)
- Should not attempt to fix missing AI trailer (same - deliberate attribution)
- Should not attempt to fix structure violations (those require architectural judgment)
- Should not auto-fix Biome 'unsafe' fixes - only 'safe' fixes. Check if biome --write respects this boundary already or if we need --apply-unsafe separately
- Should not silently succeed - always report what changed even if everything passed

OUTPUT CONTRACT:
- List every fix applied: 'Auto-applied: Biome safe fixes (2 rules), body wrapped at 72 chars'
- Then show remaining failures if any
- Exit 0 only if post-fix validation is fully clean
- Exit 1 with clear 'these require manual fix' list if anything remains

OPEN QUESTIONS FOR CODEX INPUT:
- Does 'biome check --write' apply only safe fixes or unsafe too? Need to confirm before wiring it in - we do not want --fix making semantically risky changes
- Should --fix imply --write (body wrap) automatically, or should --write remain a separate opt-in even under --fix? Lean toward --fix implies --write since the whole point is maximum automation
- Should --fix run preflight guards (README guard, docs README guard) or skip them since those are not auto-fixable anyway? Probably skip and note them separately
- What happens if Biome --write modifies a file and then structure check fails because of the modification? Edge case but possible

FRICTION LOG (real failures encountered that --fix would have prevented):
- useTemplate lint error on 'current += ' ' + word' - caught by hook, required a fix+restage cycle
- body-max-line-length on multi-sentence prose bodies - the most common failure by far, hit it on almost every substantive commit
- subject-case and header-max-length failures when drafting titles - these are NOT auto-fixable, agent must rewrite
- Multiple sequential failures because preflight only validated title (no --body), then hook caught body violations - the whole reason --body was added

IMPLEMENTATION NOTE:
The Biome fix step in --fix should reuse or mirror what run-biome-staged.mjs already does (format --write + lint). Do not duplicate that logic - call the script or extract the shared piece. Keeps the fix behavior identical between --fix and the actual commit hook.
Working scope: align preflight with bd-style agent guidance, make --verbose print full reports on failure too, surface docs README overrides, and tighten README/docs guard wording so overrides read as completed review rather than convenience bypass.

Validation run results: help envvars output confirmed in both repos; verbose failure output confirmed in both repos for missing trailer; PT Tracker long-body commitlint failure now suggests exact wrapped body and passes with --write.

title: Consider allowing import type from lib in components
description: The check-structure.mjs script blocks all lib imports in components/, including type-only imports. Type imports are erased at compile time and have zero runtime presence, so they carry no architectural cost. The rule was right to block ShareTimingSection (it called lib functions), but blocking import type from lib/types forces components to either duplicate type shapes or be restructured unnecessarily. Consider updating the script to allow import type from @/lib but continue blocking value imports. This keeps the bright line machine-checkable while removing a false positive case.
